sector_bullets.top_bullet1: Energy (XLE) surged +3.67% to lead all sectors, outpacing the S&P 500's +0.5% weekly gain by a wide margin as oil-related equities attracted the bulk of risk-on flows.
sector_bullets.top_bullet2: Communication Services (XLC) and Technology (XLK) added +1.3% and +1.2%, respectively, with mega-cap internet and semiconductor names continuing to underpin broad-based strength in growth-oriented sectors.
sector_bullets.bot_bullet1: Materials (XLB) was the week's worst-performing sector at -2.1%, pressured by softening commodity prices and a stronger dollar that weighed on metals and chemical producers.
sector_bullets.bot_bullet2: Industrials (XLI) fell -1.96% amid ongoing concerns about slowing capital expenditure cycles, while Financials (XLF) slipped -0.77% as the elevated 10-year yield of 4.57% stoked net interest margin uncertainty across bank and insurance names.

megacap_descriptions.AAPL: Closing at $315.32, a modest +0.85% gain slightly outpaced the S&P 500's +0.5% weekly advance, suggesting stable but uninspired institutional demand ahead of the next product cycle catalyst.
megacap_descriptions.MSFT: A -0.42% slip to $385.10 against a broadly positive tape indicates mild rotation out of the name, with elevated rates at 4.57% continuing to pressure valuation multiples on longer-duration software assets.
megacap_descriptions.NVDA: Surging +7.88% to close at $210.96, this was the standout momentum trade of the week, reinforcing that AI infrastructure spending narratives remain firmly intact and capable of driving outsized moves even at scale.
megacap_descriptions.AMZN: Settling at $245.34 with a +0.48% gain that tracked nearly in line with the index, the stock appears to be consolidating recent strength rather than breaking out, with cloud and advertising fundamentals offering a stable but unexciting near-term floor.
megacap_descriptions.META: An explosive +11.48% weekly rally to $669.21 — far outpacing the broader market — signals a decisive re-rating event, likely driven by earnings or ad-revenue upside that has restored conviction among large-cap growth allocators.
megacap_descriptions.SNDK: Vaulting +9.83% to $1,915.92, the move reflects deal-driven or restructuring-related re-pricing rather than broad sector momentum, and warrants scrutiny as to whether the catalyst is durable or purely event-specific.
megacap_descriptions.AMD: Edging up +1.06% to $557.89 in a week when peer NVDA gained nearly eight times as much, the relative underperformance highlights that AI semiconductor upside is still being narrowly concentrated rather than broadly distributed across the space.
megacap_descriptions.INTC: A punishing -10.11% decline to $109.84 stands as the week's clearest sector divergence signal, underscoring deepening investor skepticism about the company's competitive positioning and execution timeline versus its fabless rivals.
megacap_descriptions.MU: Drifting -0.55% to $979.30 in a week of otherwise strong semiconductor headlines, the flat-to-negative close suggests the market is awaiting fresh inventory or pricing data before committing to the next leg of the memory cycle trade.

global_status.nikkei: Trading was halted or unavailable for the week, leaving the index unchanged at 0.00 with no price discovery to report.
global_status.stoxx: European blue chips shed 2.23% to close at 6,269.97, marking one of the steeper weekly declines among developed markets and underperforming the S&P 500's modest 0.5% gain by a wide margin.
global_status.ftse: London's large-cap benchmark slid 1.7% to 10,497.29, with the index dragged lower even as a relatively subdued VIX of 15.03 suggested the selloff was driven more by domestic or sector-specific pressures than broad risk-off sentiment.
global_status.hsi: Hong Kong outpaced every other major index tracked this week, surging 2.91% to 24,030.18 and standing in stark contrast to broad weakness across European markets.

crypto_descriptions.btc: A recovery from the $61,276 weekly low to a close near $63,943 signals resilient demand at support, with bulls failing to sustain a push above the $64,598 ceiling despite a 2.24% weekly gain.
crypto_descriptions.eth: Trading in a tight $118 range between $1,712 and $1,830, the 2.07% weekly gain masked underlying indecision, with price closing at $1,793 and struggling to reclaim the $1,800 psychological level.
crypto_descriptions.sol: Underperforming the broader market by a wide margin, the 5.25% weekly decline to $77.96 stood in stark contrast to modest gains in BTC and ETH, suggesting asset-specific selling pressure rather than macro-driven weakness.
crypto_descriptions.xrp: A 2.99% decline to a $1.10 close diverged from the modest risk-on tone reflected in the S&P 500's 0.5% gain and a contained VIX of 15.03, pointing to waning speculative appetite specific to the asset.

narrative.takeaway_text: The S&P 500's modest +0.5% weekly gain masked a significant divergence under the surface, with cyclical defensives and rate-sensitive sectors bearing the brunt of a 10-year yield that crept back to 4.57% — Materials and Industrials shedding -2.1% and -1.96% respectively as the reflation/infrastructure trade unwound, while Energy's surge on the back of crude's +4.32% weekly rip and megacap tech's resilience carried the index and widened the Nasdaq-DJIA spread to over 140 basis points of relative performance. The VIX's compression to 15.03 suggests the options market is not pricing meaningful near-term tail risk despite the rates overhang, a complacency that warrants scrutiny given Euro Stoxx 50's -2.23% decline signals global growth anxiety that U.S. equities have yet to fully discount. Into next week, the positioning bias favors staying overweight Energy and large-cap Tech while remaining underweight rate-duration-exposed sectors — Financials' -0.77% despite the yield move is a particular red flag, suggesting credit concerns are offsetting the NIM benefit and making XLF a sector to avoid until the yield curve narrative clarifies.

lookahead.macro: Watch Tuesday's CPI print closely — with the 10-year yield already up 9 basis points this week to 4.57%, any upside surprise above the consensus 3.4% YoY could push yields toward the 4.70% resistance level and pressure equity multiples further. The DXY held near 101 despite modest weekly gains, suggesting dollar strength is not yet a consensus trade, but a hot inflation print could reignite that thesis and weigh on emerging market assets and commodities simultaneously.
lookahead.fed_policy: Fed speakers scheduled throughout the week, including appearances from Waller and Williams, will be scrutinized for any softening in their higher-for-longer stance given crude oil's 4.32% weekly surge adding renewed cost-push pressure to the pipeline. Markets are currently pricing fewer than two cuts for 2025, and any hawkish reaffirmation could extend the yield curve flattening trend and continue to punish rate-sensitive sectors like XLF, which already underperformed this week.
lookahead.earnings_and_catalysts: Retail earnings from Walmart and Home Depot mid-week serve as a critical real-time read on the U.S. consumer, particularly whether margin guidance reflects input cost pressure from the crude oil rally or demand softening from persistent 4.5%-plus mortgage rates. Strength in XLC this week suggests markets are still rewarding growth narratives, so any upside from consumer discretionary-adjacent names could reinforce that sector rotation and offer tactical long opportunities in communication services into month-end.
lookahead.risk_factors: The combination of VIX at 15.03 — low but no longer at complacency lows — and gold's 0.63% weekly decline signals that safe-haven demand is muted but hedging appetite may be quietly building, particularly if geopolitical risk around energy supply chains re-emerges given crude's sharp weekly move. Investors should monitor crude oil's ability to hold above the $83 level; a sustained breakout would pressure airline and transportation stocks, reignite stagflation concerns, and potentially reverse this week's thin S&P 500 gains of just 0.5% with limited breadth to absorb the shock.
